requirements.requirement: Create the three local accounts on node2 while preserving identities, primary and supplementary groups, home paths, GECOS fields, and login shells.
requirements.summary: Node2 contains mira, niko, and sana with the source UIDs/GIDs, GECOS values, /home paths, /bin/bash shells, matching private groups, and legacy-users membership. The state persisted across node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve password hashes and all password/account-aging state so existing passwords remain usable.
requirements.summary: The source passwords were proven valid at baseline. Source and destination protected shadow records match exactly, including every aging field; all accounts remain active, and Ubuntu 24.04 supports the preserved SHA-512 hashes after restart.

requirements.requirement: Migrate the complete home directories to node2 with their contents and material filesystem metadata intact.
requirements.summary: The canonical 24-entry source and destination manifests match exactly across paths, file hashes, types, symlink target, ownership, permissions, mtimes, hard-link relationships, and xattrs. The same manifest remained intact after node2 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Leave the original accounts and home directories on node1 unchanged.
requirements.summary: Node1 retained the original passwd/group records, memberships, active password and aging state, identical protected shadow state, and the identical 24-entry home manifest before and after migration and restart.

overall_summary: All four material task outcomes are satisfied. The migrated accounts, credentials, aging data, memberships, shells, and complete homes are present and persistent on node2, while node1's originals remain intact. Provider-wide restart evidence is complete and independently corroborated for both nodes.
limitations: No end-to-end PAM password login was captured on node2. Password continuity is instead established by the baseline known-password tests, exact shadow-record equivalence, destination crypt compatibility, and successful per-user shell/home checks (source-password-authentication, cmd-d7c2ebe3d8ad4778, cmd-2b32cac1570347ca).

The first node1 post-restart command exited before confirming its tar-stream home checksum (cmd-ce656e84e9ac4799). The subsequent canonical manifest check succeeded exactly and is stronger, but the earlier probe's failure cause was not isolated (cmd-e7c475fe144548c2).

operational_hygiene.summary: One unnecessary transient mutation was identified: cmd-f043385430714016 left a failed destination staging tree containing the decrypted migration archive after an incorrect archive-path check rejected valid entries. It was protected by umask 077 and fully removed by cmd-4d97d98821a04503, so nothing remained. The other failed mutating attempts were bounded and causally informed their corrections: cmd-7aa3172a5ed44219 exposed the source archive ownership problem and had an EXIT cleanup trap; cmd-f41d812874154be9 transactionally rolled back its account installation, with cmd-25d8ad0ec04d4ca9 confirming the accounts were absent before the final installation. Final checks found no migration staging, failed services, package damage, or additional network exposure. Both mandatory restart protocols had healthy baselines, acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and recovered account/home state, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot observations.
